---
title: "Readings — Design patterns, failure modes and the capstone"
---

Failure modes are best learned from papers that measured them. These show the signature of each in real data; read them with the failure table from the deck beside you.

## Start here

**Head SR, et al. (2014).** *Library construction for next-generation sequencing: overviews and challenges.* BioTechniques 56:61–77.
[doi:10.2144/000114133](https://doi.org/10.2144/000114133) — **start here**

> The blocks, in the order of a typical protocol, with what goes wrong at each. Use it to check your block list for the capstone.

**Kircher M, Sawyer S, Meyer M (2012).** *Double indexing overcomes inaccuracies in multiplex sequencing on the Illumina platform.* Nucleic Acids Research 40:e3.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkr771](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkr771) — **start here**

> The case for dual indexes, with measurements of how often a read carries the wrong one. Look for how the error is detected.

## Failure modes

**Costello M, et al. (2018).** *Characterization and remediation of sample index swaps by non-redundant dual indexing on massively parallel sequencing platforms.* BMC Genomics 19.
[doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0)

> Measured index hopping, and why unique dual indexes remove the problem. Note the rates.

**van der Valk T, et al. (2019).** *Index hopping on the Illumina HiseqX platform and its consequences for ancient DNA studies.* Molecular Ecology Resources 20:1171–1181.
[doi:10.1111/1755-0998.13009](https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.13009)

> What hopping does when samples are low in endogenous DNA: the contaminating signal can exceed the real one.

**Aird D, et al. (2011).** *Analyzing and minimizing PCR amplification bias in Illumina sequencing libraries.* Genome Biology 12:R18.
[doi:10.1186/gb-2011-12-2-r18](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2011-12-2-r18)

> The signature of over-amplification: GC bias curves. Compare them with your own coverage plots.

**Kebschull JM, Zador AM (2015).** *Sources of PCR-induced distortions in high-throughput sequencing data sets.* Nucleic Acids Research (2015).
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkv717](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv717)

> Chimeras and errors in PCR, separated by their cause.

**Lasken RS, Stockwell TB (2007).** *Mechanism of chimera formation during the multiple displacement amplification reaction.* BMC Biotechnology 7:19.
[doi:10.1186/1472-6750-7-19](https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6750-7-19)

> A mechanistic account of how a chimera forms; the same logic applies to other amplification steps.

- A vendor enzyme selection chart (polymerases, ligases, nucleases)
